hints: Determine the probability of obtaining two tails when throwing two fair coins at the same time: $p = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$.
The probability of failure (not getting two tails) is $q = 1 - p = \dfrac{3}{4}$.
The random variable $X$ represents the number of throws until the first success, which follows a geometric distribution $X \sim \mathrm{Geo}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$.
Apply the formula $\mathrm{P}(X = 7) = q^6 p = \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^6 \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$ and evaluate the result.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the single-trial success probability.
When two fair coins are thrown simultaneously, the 4 equally likely outcomes are $\{\text{HH, HT, TH, TT}\}$.
Getting two tails corresponds to the single outcome TT:
$$p = \mathrm{P}(\text{TT}) = \frac{1}{4}$$
The probability of not getting two tails on a throw is:
$$q = 1 - p = \frac{3}{4}$$

Step 2: Identify the distribution of $X$.
The random variable $X$ is the number of independent trials required up to and including the first success. This follows a geometric distribution:
$$X \sim \mathrm{Geo}(p) = \mathrm{Geo}\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)$$

Step 3: Calculate $\mathrm{P}(X = 7)$.
For the first success to occur on the 7th throw, the first 6 throws must be failures and the 7th throw must be a success:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 7) = q^6 p = \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^6 \left(\frac{1}{4}\right)$$

Step 4: Compute the numerical value:
$$\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^6 = \frac{3^6}{4^6} = \frac{729}{4096}$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 7) = \frac{729}{4096 \times 4} = \frac{729}{16384} \approx 0.0444949 \dots$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.0445$ (or exact fraction $\frac{729}{16384}$).

hints: In a geometric distribution, $X > 9$ means that the first 9 throws must all result in failure (no two tails).
Use the geometric tail formula $\mathrm{P}(X > n) = q^n$, where $q = \dfrac{3}{4}$ and $n = 9$.
Evaluate $\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^9$ as an exact fraction or decimal to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Understand the tail probability of a geometric distribution.
The event that it takes more than 9 throws to obtain the first success means that no success occurred in the first 9 throws.
In other words, throw 1 through throw 9 all resulted in failures:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 9) = \mathrm{P}(\text{failure on first 9 throws})$$

Step 2: Apply the independence of trials.
Because each throw of the two coins is independent with failure probability $q = \frac{3}{4}$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 9) = q^9 = \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^9$$

Step 3: Calculate the value:
$$3^9 = 19683$$
$$4^9 = 262144$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 9) = \frac{19683}{262144} \approx 0.07508468 \dots$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.0751$ (or exact fraction $\frac{19683}{262144}$).
